news.2026-10-31-canada-ue-membre-associe: Canada wants to become the European Union's first "associate member" by June 2027
At the EU-Canada summit in Montreal, Mark Carney set a goal: to conclude by June 2027 talks on a new kind of tie with the Union, halfway between partner and member.
At the EU-Canada summit in Montreal, Prime Minister Mark Carney said he wants to conclude by June 2027 the negotiations to make Canada the European Union's first "associate member" [1][2].

He speaks of "the deepest possible partnership short of accession, because of our geography"; yet the word "associate" does not appear in the summit's final statement, as Germany objected to it [2][3].
The idea came from Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission, who proposed it on 16 September in her State of the Union speech [4].
Key point: this status does not exist yet. It will have to be invented and accepted by the Union's 27 countries, and Canada's Parliament will have to vote [2][3].

For Canada, it is a way to depend less on its big American neighbour, in the middle of a trade war with Washington [3]. For Europe, it is one more ally just as its relations with the United States grow tense [3]. An associate member would, however, have no European citizenship, no free movement, no commissioner and no vote in the Union's institutions [5].

If the project succeeds, trade between Europe and Canada would become even simpler: goods, studies, work, defence. And it is one more sign that alliances are being redrawn in the face of US trade policy [3][5].
